text:
Maya R: Quick design check — the new canary traffic 'heatmap' on the rollout timeline looks great visually but I think the contrast between 10% and 30% bins is too subtle, especially for colorblind users. :eyes:
Ethan: Agree. I can barely tell 10 vs 30 on my laptop outside. Maybe we need a pattern or a stronger hue shift.
Lee T: Pattern overlay is good for print/accessibility, but it makes the mini-map noisy at 320px. Would recommend stronger saturation + dashed pattern only at smaller widths.
Priya S: Also important: the percentage chip reads just the number visually, but screen readers need context. Current aria-label is "10%" — should be "Canary traffic: 10 percent". a11y-bot flagged it in the QA run.
a11y-bot: automated-check: aria-label missing context on 3 elements — severity: medium. Suggest `role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"` for the timeline summary when allocations change.
Sam G: For rollback CTA copy: current modal says "Rollback" and the confirm button is "Yes, rollback" — feels risky. Suggest changing confirm to "Confirm rollback to v.X" and add the time window info. Short and explicit.
Maya R: Good call. Also thinking about microcopy for canary hover: we show "10% to canary" — can we change to "10% traffic to canary (approx. 12 requests/sec)" when we have throughput data? That helps PMs decide quickly.
Ethan: Backend can surface a live-estimate metric. Let's make it optional so it falls back to just percent when unavailable. UI should not shift layout when metric appears.
Lee T: Keyboard focus: when you TAB into the timeline scrubber, the focused variant pill needs a visible ring and an accessible name that reads variant + allocation, e.g., "variant blue: 10 percent". Also ensure the mini-scrubber's drag handle has `aria-grabbed` states.
Priya S: On colors — recommend we use Okabe-Ito palette as a baseline for categorical variants, then apply a sequential ramp for allocation heat. That handles deuteranopia better.
Sam G: UX tradeoff: stronger colors improve contrast but might make A/B bands feel aggressive. Can we try a subtle drop shadow instead of ramp contrast for the selected variant?
Maya R: Let's prototype two comps: (A) stronger sequential ramp + pattern fallback, (B) current ramp + subtle drop shadow on selection. I'll add both to figma.
Ethan: FYI, I pushed a small CSS fallback for pattern in storybook:
```
.timeline-heatmap { background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, #eaf2ff, #1f6feb); }
.timeline-heatmap.pattern { background-image: url('/patterns/diagonals.svg'); }
```
Lee T: Looks good. Ensure the SVG pattern uses `aria-hidden=true` and is included as background to avoid noise for screen readers.
Priya S: One last copy nudge — rollback confirmation should include an explicit note: "This will route new traffic to the selected version. Current requests will finish on the old version." That reduces ambiguity.
Maya R: Perfect. Action items: I will upload two comps to the thread, Ethan will add the live-estimate toggle, Lee will add focus ring + aria-grabbed, Priya will update copy and a11y labels, Sam will test visual weight with PMs. Thanks! :thumbsup:
